articles.title: UH receives $2M to develop AI tools for food safety
articles.description: UH receives $2M to develop AI tools for food safety Hawaii News Now
articles.description_html: UH receives $2M to develop AI tools for food safety  Hawaii News Now
articles.article_title: UH receives $2M to develop AI tools for food safety
articles.heading: UH receives $2M to develop AI tools for food safety
articles.summary: UH Manoa received $2M in federal funds to develop AI-based technology that can detect environmental threats to livestock, crops, and aquaculture.
articles.content:
UH receives $2M to develop AI tools for food safety
HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - The University of Hawaii at Manoa has received federal funding to develop new tools aimed at protecting food production systems.
UH Manoa received $2 million from the National Science Foundation to help create artificial intelligence-based technology that can detect environmental threats before they become larger problems.
The four-year project is being led by UH Manoa in partnership with the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.
Researchers will combine AI with environmental sampling, genetic analysis and chemical testing to identify potential risks to aquaculture, livestock and agricultural systems.
“So we want to make sure that the foods they are producing are clean and safe to consume,” said project principal investigator Tao Yan. “So that’s good for the farmers and also good for the consumers.”
The project comes as public health officials continue investigating foodborne illnesses tied to Cyclospora.
“Right now we look at the Cyclospora problem, we know it after people have already consumed the food,” Yan said. “So the new technology, AI-based, the tools that we’re trying to develop, will aim to detect those problems before they manifest into bigger problems like we have today.”
Researchers will initially test the technology in aquaculture and beef cattle operations.
The project will also provide research opportunities for students and junior faculty while working with industry partners, regulators and communities.
The full NSF award totals $4 million, with UH receiving half of the funding.

articles.article_title: Men's Soccer Draws with Western Connecticut, 0-0 - Stevens Institute of Technology Athletics
articles.heading: Stevens Institute of Technology Athletics
articles.summary: Danbury, Conn. – The Stevens Institute of Technology men's soccer team Western Connecticut State University to a 0-0 draw Saturday evening.
articles.content:
Danbury, Conn.
– The Stevens Institute of Technology men's soccer team Western Connecticut State University to a 0-0 draw Saturday evening.

Stevens (1-0-1) held a 13-4 advantage in shots and a 9-2 edge in corner kicks, including a 9-1 advantage in shots over the final 45 minutes.

HOW IT HAPPENED
Western Connecticut generated the first two attempts of the contest before Stevens nearly broke through in the 11th minute.
Martin Fields
connected on a header that struck the post to keep the match scoreless.
Emerson Kekesi
followed with attempts in the 16th and 19th minutes as the Ducks began to establish themselves in the attacking third. Stevens earned three corner kicks during the opening half before
Lucas Mendes
put the Ducks' first shot on goal in the 34th minute, forcing a save from the goalkeeper.

Stevens increased the pressure immediately after halftime. Kekesi directed a header on goal in the 50th minute before
Matthew Murillo
followed with an attempt less than 20 seconds later. The Ducks then earned four corner kicks over the next six minutes but were unable to turn the opportunities into the opening goal. The Wolves registered their only shot on goal in the 62nd minute when Boyke, was tested, but he made the save to preserve the scoreless contest.

The Ducks continued to push forward and came within inches of taking the lead in the 75th minute. Following a Stevens corner,
Joey Bucchere
connected on a header that struck the crossbar. Murillo forced another Smith save in the 79th minute before Fields generated three chances over a five-minute stretch. Fields sent a header wide in the 81st minute before putting headers on target in the 84th and 86th minutes, with Smith turning away both attempts.

INSIDE THE BOX SCORE
- The Ducks earned nine corner kicks compared to two for the home side, including a 6-2 edge in the second half.
- Fields finished with a match-high four shots and put two on goal. Kekesi added three shots, while Murillo recorded two.
- Boyke played all 90 minutes and made one save to earn the clean sheet.
- Stevens' defense did not allow a shot on goal until the 62nd minute and surrendered just one total attempt in the second half.
UP NEXT
Stevens returns to Hoboken for its 2026 home opener on Tuesday, Sept. 8, when the Ducks welcome Skidmore College to the DeBaun Athletic Complex. Opening kick is scheduled for 7:30 p.m.

articles.article_title: A&M–Central Texas’ Engineering Technology Program receives ABET accreditation
articles.heading: A&M–Central Texas’ Engineering Technology Program receives ABET accreditation
articles.summary: The bachelor’s degree program in mechanical engineering technology (MET) at Texas A&M University–Central Texas in Killeen has been accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, a nonprofit, certified
articles.content:
The bachelor’s degree program in mechanical engineering technology (MET) at Texas A&M University–Central Texas in Killeen has been accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, a nonprofit, certified quality assurance organization. Through the accreditation of academic programs, recognition of credentials and assessment of student learning, ABET supports excellence in education worldwide.
ABET accreditation assures that programs meet standards to produce graduates ready to enter critical technical fields that are leading the way in innovation and emerging technologies and anticipating the welfare and safety needs of the public.
Associate professor of engineering, Taylor Harvey, said this accreditation is a tremendous benefit to students in the MET program.
“It validates the strength of the education our program provides and confirms that our students graduate with the technical knowledge, practical skills, and hand-on experience they need to succeed in the workplace,” Harvey said.
Sought worldwide, ABET’s voluntary peer-review process is highly respected because it adds critical value to academic programs in the technical disciplines, where quality, precision and safety are of the utmost importance.
Developed by technical professionals from ABET’s member societies, ABET criteria focus on what students experience and learn. ABET accreditation reviews look at program curricula, faculty, facilities and institutional support and are conducted by teams of highly skilled professionals from industry, academia and government, with expertise in the ABET disciplines.
ABET currently accredits 4,773 programs at 930 colleges and universities in 41 countries and areas as of Oct. 1, 2024.
More information about ABET, its member societies and the accreditation criteria used to evaluate programs can be found at www.abet.org.
For more information about the bachelor’s degree program in mechanical engineering technology at A&M–Central Texas, visit tamuct.edu.

Microchip Technology (MCHP) Teams With Marelli As Its Undervalued Narrative Stays In Focus
Microchip Technology (MCHP) is back in focus after teaming up with Marelli on an open standard solution that streams graphics and video from a vehicle central computer directly to in car displays using ASA Motion Link.
For investors, that product news sits alongside a mixed trading picture, with Microchip Technology’s share price now at US$74.17 and a year to date share price return of 14.06%, together with a 1 year total shareholder return of 15.46%. The weaker 90 day share price return of 16.04% suggests recent momentum has cooled, even as longer term total shareholder returns over 3 and 5 years remain positive.
Scan how Microchip Technology's automotive push compares to other chipmakers gearing up for software defined vehicles with our curated 55 AI infrastructure stocks.
Microchip Technology looks like a solid embedded systems and automotive supplier, and the Marelli collaboration adds another proof point. The live question now is whether that strength is already fully reflected in the US$74 share price.
Most Popular Narrative: 31.7% Undervalued
Microchip Technology's most followed narrative pegs fair value at $108.64, well above the recent $74.17 close, which puts the current share price in context.
The accelerating adoption of edge computing and proliferation of AI-enabled, connected devices is fueling demand for Microchip's portfolio of microcontrollers, analog, and FPGA solutions, including recent design wins in AI/data center infrastructure and the expansion into secure, power-efficient edge AI products, supporting incremental revenue opportunities as these trends continue.
Read the complete narrative. Read the complete narrative.
Want to see what underpins that higher fair value for Microchip Technology? The narrative leans heavily on future earnings power, richer margins, and a different profit multiple than today. The exact mix of revenue growth, profitability, and required return is where the story really gets interesting.
At the core of this narrative is a model that assumes Microchip Technology can grow its top line and expand profit margins over several years, with earnings reaching the low single digit billions and a P/E that is lower than the current US semiconductor industry average. The fair value also reflects a discount rate of 11.83%, which is the return investors might require to hold the stock given its risks and cash flow profile. That combination of higher earnings, healthier margins, and a defined required return is what leads to the $108.64 figure.
Result: Fair Value of $108.64 (UNDERVALUED)
Have a read of the narrative in full and understand what's behind the forecasts.
However, Microchip Technology still faces elevated inventory and substantial debt, which could pressure margins and limit flexibility if end market demand softens again.
Find out about the key risks to this Microchip Technology narrative.
Another View on Microchip Technology's Valuation
The analyst narrative points to Microchip Technology trading below a fair value of $108.64, yet the current P/E of about 109.7x tells a different story. That multiple is far higher than peers at 61.4x, the US semiconductor industry at 47.2x, and a fair ratio of 35.5x. This comparison suggests considerable valuation risk if sentiment cools.
When a stock carries a P/E that far above both its industry and an estimated fair ratio, it often means expectations are already very high. The key question for investors is whether Microchip Technology can deliver enough earnings growth to support that premium, or if the market could eventually move closer to the fair ratio.

Micron Technology (MU) CEO Sanjay Mehrotra Earns Taipei Supply Chain Award
- Micron Technology (NasdaqGS:MU) CEO Sanjay Mehrotra received the Medal of Economic Contribution at the Semicon Network Summit 2026 in Taipei for work on U.S. Taiwan semiconductor cooperation.
- The award highlights Micron's role in cross border chip supply chain coordination and AI era technology collaboration.
- The summit focused on global semiconductor supply resilience and international partnerships, areas that are closely watched by investors assessing geopolitical exposure.
Micron is one of several companies tied to the build out of AI related chip infrastructure, so it can be useful to view this news alongside a broader group of exposed stocks through 55 AI infrastructure stocks.
Micron Technology is a US based semiconductor company that designs and manufactures memory and storage products used in devices and data centers across regions including Taiwan, Japan, Mainland China, Hong Kong, Europe, and the United States. Its global manufacturing and sales footprint helps explain why cross border supply chain cooperation is highly relevant for the business.
Why this U.S. Taiwan recognition matters for Micron Technology’s AI supply story
For Micron Technology investors, this award is less about prestige and more about whether the AI focused memory Narrative can rely on stable cross border execution. The current story leans heavily on tight DRAM and HBM supply, long term contracts and heavy investment in advanced nodes and capacity across the U.S., Taiwan, Japan and other regions. Formal recognition of Sanjay Mehrotra’s role in U.S. Taiwan cooperation points to work behind the scenes on supply chain access and government relationships, which speaks directly to the geopolitical and supply disruption risks highlighted in the Narrative.
If we take a look at the community Narrative for Micron Technology, we can see how this news fits into the bigger investment story.
The practical test is what Micron’s next major updates say about operations and contracts tied to Taiwan. Watch upcoming earnings commentary and production guidance for any detail on cross border capacity plans, HBM and DRAM output allocation and how those feed into the multi year Strategic Customer Agreements that underpin AI data center demand expectations.
For the full picture including more risks and rewards, check out the complete Micron Technology analysis.

articles.content:
ALPR technology helps locate suspect in Lorena robbery case
LORENA, Texas (KWTX) - Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALPR) technology played a vital role in finding a suspect in a Lorena robbery case, Chief Scott Holt said in a statement.
At 9:24 p.m. Friday, Lorena officers were dispatched to 12016 I-35, in reference to a robbery call.
Upon arrival, the responding officer ensured the victim’s safety and began collecting information to send to area law enforcement agencies.
According to the statement, it was determined the suspect stole the victim’s vehicle.
During the theft, the victim suffered non-life-threatening injuries, elevating the offense to robbery, the statement reads.
Chief Holt said the victim denied medical treatment and was released to family on scene.
Within an hour and a half of the initial 911 call, the suspect was located in the DFW area using ALPR technology, according to the statement. Neither the victim nor the suspect was from Central Texas.
“This successful resolution was made possible through the outstanding collaborative effort of Lorena officers and our external partners, who worked efficiently and seamlessly throughout the investigation,” Chief Holt said in his statement.
According to Lorena Police, this is an isolated incident and there is no threat to public safety.
This is a developing story. No further details are available.

articles.heading: Stevens Institute of Technology Athletics
articles.summary: Farmingdale, N.Y. – Victoria Parelli scored her first goal of the season as the Stevens Institute of Technology women's soccer team battled Westfield State University
articles.content:
Farmingdale, N.Y.
–
Victoria Parelli
scored her first goal of the season as the Stevens Institute of Technology women's soccer team battled Westfield State University to a 1-1 draw on Saturday afternoon at Rams Field.

The Ducks (0-0-1) controlled much of the contest, outshooting Westfield State 30-5 and holding a 13-1 advantage in corner kicks, but the Owls found an equalizer in the 73rd minute to earn the draw.

HOW IT HAPPENED
Stevens controlled possession from the opening whistle, earning a pair of corner kicks in the opening eight minutes before
Abby Davis
registered the Ducks' first shot of the afternoon in the 14th minute. The Ducks continued to generate opportunities throughout the opening half, with
Alana Odom
,
Kaitlyn Pettit
,
Sophia Carr
,
Hanna Kusinski
and Parelli all recording attempts as Stevens kept Westfield State pinned in its defensive half for long stretches.

Olivia Hoover
provided the first shot on goal in the 32nd minute, forcing the Westfield State goalkeeper into a save. Stevens continued to apply pressure before finally breaking through with just over four minutes remaining in the half. Parelli put the Ducks ahead in the 41
st
minute mark, firing a shot from 28 yards out into the upper-right corner for her first goal of the season. The goal sent Stevens into halftime with a 1-0 advantage after holding an 11-1 edge in shots and a 4-0 advantage in corner kicks over the opening 45 minutes.

Stevens immediately went back on the attack following halftime.
Sophia Murphy
recorded three attempts over the opening 11 minutes of the second half, including an effort in the 51st minute that was stopped by Santucci. Hoover continued to create chances after reentering the match, recording three shots between the 59th and 68th minutes. She forced Santucci into a save in the 68th minute before another attempt seconds later was cleared off the line by the Owls.

Despite Stevens controlling the run of play, Westfield State found the equalizer in the 73
rd
minute to pull the Owls even at 1-1. The Ducks responded by pushing forward in search of the go-ahead goal. Odom put an attempt on target in the 81st minute, while Stevens earned six corner kicks over the final 11 minutes of regulation. Murphy registered four shots over the final six minutes and
Taylor Truglia
added an attempt in the 89th, but the Ducks were unable to find the deciding goal.

INSIDE THE NUMBERS
- The Ducks put seven attempts on goal while limiting Westfield State to just one shot on target.
- Hoover led the offensive attack with a match-high eight shots, including three on goal, while Murphy finished with six attempts.
- Davis recorded three shots, while Parelli, Odom, Pettit, Kusinski and Carr each added two.
- Parelli's goal was the first of her season and came on one of her two attempts in 38 minutes off the bench.
- Lucy Smith played all 90 minutes in goal for the Ducks.
UP NEXT
Stevens returns to Rams Field on Sunday when the Ducks face Plattsburgh State at 11 a.m. to close out their two-match trip to Farmingdale.

HOW IT HAPPENED

Stevens controlled possession from the opening whistle, earning a pair of corner kicks in the opening eight minutes before

Abby Davis

registered the Ducks' first shot of the afternoon in the 14th minute. The Ducks continued to generate opportunities throughout the opening half, with

Alana Odom

,

Kaitlyn Pettit

,

Sophia Carr

,

Hanna Kusinski

and Parelli all recording attempts as Stevens kept Westfield State pinned in its defensive half for long stretches.  

Olivia Hoover

provided the first shot on goal in the 32nd minute, forcing the Westfield State goalkeeper into a save. Stevens continued to apply pressure before finally breaking through with just over four minutes remaining in the half. Parelli put the Ducks ahead in the 41

st

 minute mark, firing a shot from 28 yards out into the upper-right corner for her first goal of the season. The goal sent Stevens into halftime with a 1-0 advantage after holding an 11-1 edge in shots and a 4-0 advantage in corner kicks over the opening 45 minutes.  

Stevens immediately went back on the attack following halftime.

Sophia Murphy

recorded three attempts over the opening 11 minutes of the second half, including an effort in the 51st minute that was stopped by Santucci. Hoover continued to create chances after reentering the match, recording three shots between the 59th and 68th minutes. She forced Santucci into a save in the 68th minute before another attempt seconds later was cleared off the line by the Owls.  

Despite Stevens controlling the run of play, Westfield State found the equalizer in the 73

rd

 minute to pull the Owls even at 1-1. The Ducks responded by pushing forward in search of the go-ahead goal. Odom put an attempt on target in the 81st minute, while Stevens earned six corner kicks over the final 11 minutes of regulation. Murphy registered four shots over the final six minutes and

Taylor Truglia

added an attempt in the 89th, but the Ducks were unable to find the deciding goal.  

INSIDE THE NUMBERS
  • The Ducks put seven attempts on goal while limiting Westfield State to just one shot on target.
  • Hoover led the offensive attack with a match-high eight shots, including three on goal, while Murphy finished with six attempts. 
  • Davis recorded three shots, while Parelli, Odom, Pettit, Kusinski and Carr each added two.
  • Parelli's goal was the first of her season and came on one of her two attempts in 38 minutes off the bench.
  • Lucy Smith played all 90 minutes in goal for the Ducks.
UP NEXT

Stevens returns to Rams Field on Sunday when the Ducks face Plattsburgh State at 11 a.m. to close out their two-match trip to Farmingdale.

articles.title: The rise of the anti-social American
articles.description: The rise of the anti-social American The Hill
articles.description_html: The rise of the anti-social American  The Hill
articles.article_title: The rise of the anti-social American
articles.heading: The rise of the anti-social American
articles.summary: Writer John Mac Ghlionn argues that modern American life has shifted toward extreme isolation and digital dependency, sacrificing genuine human connection for technological convenience.
articles.content:
The American welcome mat used to mean something; now it’s just the designated drop-off zone for the Amazon courier. There was a time, not that long ago, when the average suburban street was full of unannounced drop-ins, the smell of burning charcoal, and scattered lawn chairs. Today, neighborhoods possess the lifeless feel of a well-maintained cemetery. The modern American Dream is best described as a private bunker where the outside world arrives entirely in a cardboard box or a fiber-optic cable.
Americans now spend considerably less time with other people than they did 20 years ago. This is a magnificent triumph of optimization. The human animal is notoriously unreliable. He’s prone to bad breath, political rants, and requests to help move heavy furniture. Eliminating the physical neighbor in favor of a digital stream is a sensible defense mechanism. The local bar, once a breeding ground for scandalous gossip and collective hangovers, has been soundly defeated by DoorDash and a high-definition TV. America has achieved the pinnacle of individual autonomy: the right to die alone in a perfectly temperature-controlled living room.
The modern economy operates on the premise that human contact is a design flaw. Up until the early 2000s, buying a loaf of bread required a verbal exchange with a cashier who might comment on the weather. Today, self-checkout kiosks and gig-economy couriers ensure that a citizen could survive for six consecutive months without uttering a single syllable to another member of the species. The delivery driver leaves the paper bag on the porch, rings the bell, and vanishes into the bushes like a timid woodland creature. This arrangement represents the peak of convenience, but at a cost so severe that it reduces human interaction to a transaction of mutual avoidance.
This structural shift toward complete insulation has naturally changed how Americans allocate their emotional resources. The supposedly outdated concept of friendship required actual physical stamina. It demanded driving across town, listening to tedious stories about a stranger’s root canal, and pretending to enjoy terrible homemade casserole. The digital landscape solved this problem by converting relationships into a currency of metrics. A person can now maintain five hundred “connections” from the comfort of a porcelain toilet seat. It’s now possible to receive a constant stream of validation without the exhausting requirement of showing up at a hospital bedside or helping someone paint their garage. It is an exquisite system of emotional capitalism in which everyone is an investor and no one performs the actual labor.
The logical conclusion of this optimization is as depressing as it is inevitable. Millions of citizens now spend their evenings conversing with large language models (LLMs), pouring their deepest fears into software that could ultimately use those vulnerabilities to destroy them. The machine is the perfect companion. It never interrupts, and it will never ask to borrow $50. It provides the illusion of intimacy without the terrifying risk of human rejection. A generation raised on the predictable feedback loops of video games has found its ultimate match: a partner that is literally programmed to agree with everything they say.
This reliance on artificial empathy reflects a broader cultural realization that human relationships are simply too taxing to maintain. Between skyrocketing rent and the sheer exhaustion of everyday life, a chatbot quickly becomes the easiest companion. The traditional pillars of community — the local church, the bowling league, the union hall — all required an investment of time, vulnerability and occasionally a membership fee. The algorithm requires only your eyeballs.
Even leisure activities have been thoroughly scrubbed of any genuine spontaneity. The casual afternoon stroll or the unrecorded vacation is an extinct concept. Every minute of non-work time must be weaponized for personal branding, tracked via GPS, or cataloged for public consumption. A meal is no longer a source of nutrition but a piece of content that must be styled, lit, and uploaded to prove to an indifferent audience that the consumer is alive and very much enjoying themselves. The act of living has become a corporate marketing campaign managed by a staff of one.
The ultimate casualty of this hyper-efficient lifestyle is the concept of unmonetized time. Spending three hours sitting on a porch talking about nothing is an economic absurdity in a culture that demands constant self-improvement and digital engagement. Americans, like much of modern society, are constantly connected to the world yet increasingly detached from the floorboards beneath their feet. The American experiment began with the pursuit of liberty and has culminated in the freedom to sit in an empty room, stare at a screen, and beg a box of wires for a digital pat on the head. America may still be the greatest nation on the planet, but it’s fast becoming a nation of strangers.
John Mac Ghlionn is a writer and researcher who explores culture, society and the impact of technology on daily life.

Spending three hours sitting on a porch talking about nothing is an economic absurdity in a culture that demands constant self-improvement and digital engagement. Americans, like much of modern society, are constantly connected to the world yet increasingly detached from the floorboards beneath their feet. The American experiment began with the pursuit of liberty and has culminated in the freedom to sit in an empty room, stare at a screen, and beg a box of wires for a digital pat on the head. America may still be the greatest nation on the planet, but it’s fast becoming a nation of strangers.

John Mac Ghlionn is a writer and researcher who explores culture, society and the impact of technology on daily life.

articles.description: Blue Owl Technology Finance Closes $150 Million Private Placement Of 7.60% Senior Unsecured Notes Pulse 2.0
articles.description_html: Blue Owl Technology Finance Closes $150 Million Private Placement Of 7.60% Senior Unsecured Notes  Pulse 2.0
articles.article_title: Blue Owl Technology Finance Closes $150 Million Private Placement Of 7.60% Senior Unsecured Notes
articles.heading: Blue Owl Technology Finance Closes $150 Million Private Placement Of 7.60% Senior Unsecured Notes
articles.summary: Blue Owl Technology Finance Corp. has closed a $150 million private placement of 7.60% senior unsecured notes due September 3, 2032, marking its third financing since June 30.
articles.content:
Blue Owl Technology Finance Corp. has closed a $150 million private placement of 7.60% senior unsecured notes due September 3, 2032, marking its third financing since June 30.
The latest transaction brings the business development company’s total debt financing raised since the end of the second quarter to $800 million.
In August, Blue Owl Technology Finance issued an additional $400 million of its 6.500% notes due 2029.
The company also raised $250 million through a special purpose vehicle facility secured by a pool of portfolio investments.
During the second quarter, OTF separately issued $500 million of 6.500% notes due 2029, added $150 million in secured financing and extended its $2.7 billion revolving credit facility.
Every existing banking partner renewed its revolving credit commitment, while the company also added a new lending relationship.
OTF ended the quarter with more than $2 billion of cash and available capacity across its credit facilities.
The additional capital is intended to diversify the company’s funding base and provide greater flexibility to expand its technology investment portfolio.
As of June 30, 2026, Blue Owl Technology Finance had investments in 205 portfolio companies with an aggregate fair value of $14.7 billion.
The company focuses primarily on debt and equity investments in U.S. technology-related companies, with an emphasis on software.
KEY QUOTE:
“OTF’s portfolio continues to perform well, with one of the lowest non-accrual rates in the BDC sector, and we continue to see strong support from both debt investors and our bank partners. We have raised $800 million of debt financing since quarter-end through unsecured notes and an SPV facility, which further strengthens and diversifies our funding base. This added flexibility positions us to grow the portfolio and capitalize on an increasingly attractive environment for technology investing while maintaining our underwriting discipline that has defined OTF’s performance.”
Craig W. Packer, Chief Executive Officer of Blue Owl Technology Finance Corp.

articles.title: Hangzhou: blending ancient China with cutting-edge technology
articles.description: Hangzhou: blending ancient China with cutting-edge technology The Jerusalem Post
articles.description_html: Hangzhou: blending ancient China with cutting-edge technology  The Jerusalem Post
articles.article_title: Hangzhou: blending ancient China with cutting-edge technology | The Jerusalem Post
articles.heading: Hangzhou offers a glimpse of China’s journey from silk to silicon
articles.summary: A journey through Hangzhou and Zhejiang reveals a China embracing both its ancient heritage and a high-tech future, from tea fields and historic canals to AI and robotics.
articles.content:
Hangzhou may be celebrated by leisure travelers for its trio of UNESCO World Heritage Sites, but for Western visitors making the journey today, it is likely household names from the tech sphere that ring most familiar. Chief among them is e-commerce giant Alibaba and its global subsidiary, AliExpress.
For the past three decades, these titans have come to symbolize Hangzhou’s meteoric ascent as a powerhouse of innovation, transforming both the urban landscape and the local community.
While nature still frames the metropolis, encircled as it is by lush forested hills, serene lakes, and winding rivers, this bustling city of 13 million souls has evolved far beyond its picturesque geography. Today, it stands proudly as a magnet for cutting-edge technological investment, forward-thinking educational initiatives, and top-tier IT talent drawn from every corner of the globe.
The Wensan Future Technology Experience Center is the perfect starting point for understanding how far technology has come and where it’s likely to go. Dozens of robots and AI-based technologies perform practical everyday tasks as well as entertaining activities in this visitor center. From exoskeletons to fighting robots, one can experience the very best that Hangzhou and China have to offer in this hands-on experience.
The headquarters of Alibaba affords another view into the world of hi-tech in China. In 1999, Jack Ma and 17 friends created a small company that eventually became Alibaba. Today, the group employs around 200,000 people around the world, across a variety of brands and subsidiaries, and has a whopping $140-billion turnover.
AliExpress, familiar to pretty much all Israelis, is just one part of this mega-corporation’s influence on international commerce, finance, and trade. Indeed, the company enjoys a strong investment relationship with Israel, particularly via its collaboration with Jerusalem Venture Partners.
The company’s sprawling visitor center offers a peek into the life of Ma and his colleagues through explanatory panels in a huge atrium, which is surrounded by offices of the conglomerate. Nestled at the center of the atrium is a replica of the Hangzhou apartment where the company began.
Among the technologies on display and indeed in practical use in the headquarters is facial recognition for vending machines. Simply looking at the machine engages an unlocking mechanism, items are removed, and the purchase price is automatically debited from the bank account, with a receipt automatically appearing on one’s phone.
“This is a glimpse into the future,” notes tour guide Carl Gao as the system clears another transaction. “These technologies are here now and will be everywhere soon.”
Inspiration by the water
Just steps from the urban rush lies West Lake, a tranquil expanse of water that has inspired travelers for centuries, balancing history with everyday life. In the morning, locals practice Tai Chi by the water and traditional musicians play in the pavilions, while just minutes away, the modern city hums along.
Among the historical landmarks surrounding the water is the Broken Bridge, situated at the end of the Bai Causeway. Despite its name, the bridge is structurally intact and derives its identity from an optical illusion created in winter when melting snow clears unevenly on its arch, making parts of it appear disconnected.
Historically, it served as the primary setting for the famous romantic tragedy of the White Snake, symbolizing enduring devotion and the meeting place of myth and reality.
Further out on the water stand the Three Pools Mirroring the Moon, located on a small artificial island in the southern sector of the lake. This site features three hollow stone mini-pagodas erected during the Ming Dynasty, designed with holes that allow candlelight to mix with moonlight on autumn nights.
Today, the location represents classical Chinese garden design and holds national recognition as the imagery featured on the back of the Chinese one-yuan banknote.
Overlooking the southern shore stands the Leifeng Pagoda, originally built in the 10th century by the King of Wuyue to consecrate Buddhist relics and celebrate a royal birth.
Although the original structure collapsed in 1924 due to structural decay and relic scavenging, a modern reconstruction now houses the old ruins beneath protective glass while offering a comprehensive museum space. The tower symbolizes the turbulent intersection of historical preservation and modern architectural rebuilding, providing an elevated vantage point over the entire lake basin.
West Lake sits right on the edge of the city, serving as a gateway to the broader, picture-postcard beauty of Zhejiang province.
The historic Silk Road
Some 64 million people call this wider region home, yet much of the landscape remains covered by cultivated tea plantations, mulberry bushes, and wilder vegetation climbing over mountains, hills, and a flat river delta. For centuries, tea, silk, and ceramics served as the major Chinese goods exported westward along the historic Silk Road toward Istanbul and Rome.
Today, the province also produces the deliciously fresh Nongfu Spring bottled water, a brand associated with sourcing water from protected natural environments, including the Thousand Island Lake area.
At its visitors’ center, one can observe highly automated production systems designed to bottle and distribute water and a variety of the brand’s other beverages, which include teas, vitamin drinks, and juice products, on a national scale.
The region is blessed with an ample water supply. Zhejiang features a humid subtropical monsoon climate, receiving high annual rainfall that typically ranges between 1,000 and 1,900 mm, roughly 39 to 75 inches, depending on the specific terrain.
Its often wide or powerful rivers are not only a vital source of water but also a major engine for energy. The Xin’an River Hydropower Station stands as one of the landmark engineering projects of modern China, playing an essential role in regional development by generating electricity and managing water resources to support economic growth across Zhejiang.
The project also led to the creation of the vast Thousand Island Lake reservoir, where visitors today can witness firsthand China’s ongoing efforts to balance infrastructure, industry, and environmental stewardship.
The lakeside town of Chun’an
Leaving the dam behind, the road winds along the shoreline toward Chun’an, offering wide, striking vistas across the vast lake. The surrounding hills are mostly blanketed in dense trees that give the landscape a textured, rounded look, occasionally interrupted by patches of tea plantations.
Amid the stunning scenery, a solitary fisherman stands balanced on a long, flat wooden boat, net in hand, carrying on a traditional way of life on waters that were shaped just decades ago by this modern, seemingly never-ending reservoir.
As daylight begins to fade, the lakeside town of Chun’an offers an ideal stopping point for a sunset dinner and an overnight stay. Waterfront restaurants serve fresh catches alongside local specialties, providing a relaxed atmosphere as the sky turns orange and purple over the water. It is a quiet place to rest before continuing the journey.
An hour west of Chun’an lies Xiajiang. Tucked into the hills of Zhejiang province, the village feels less like a traditional ancient hamlet and more like a carefully polished showcase. Decades ago, it was a typical, impoverished mountainside community, but heavy government investment turned it into a poster child for rural modernization.
Today, Xiajiang features neat rows of uniform whitewashed guesthouses, pristine stone paths, and an immaculate river running through the center, functioning almost as an open-air exhibition of modern Chinese country life where visitors come to see how rural tourism and state-backed revitalization intersect. Farmers dry hot peppers and corn kernels on the sidewalks and squares, just as their ancestors did, before the tourists arrived.
Wuzhen lies to the north of Hangzhou, on the way to Shanghai. It’s a canal town that wears its history on its sleeve, yet runs with the precision of a modern theme park. Located in the northern reaches of Zhejiang, this ancient water settlement dates back well over a thousand years, originally serving as a vital trading post where boats navigated a dense web of stone-lined waterways.
Today, it stands as one of China’s most famous preserved historic towns, divided administratively into distinct zones that cater directly to cultural tourists and conference-goers alike, while also taking into account the life patterns of its citizens.
Approaching the historic core, the landscape shifts abruptly from modern concrete highways to a labyrinth of weathered gray-brick buildings, black-tiled roofs, and crisscrossing arched stone bridges.
The water of the canal system laps directly against the foundations of two-story wooden houses; their balconies draped with laundry and traditional lanterns swaying gently in the breeze. Flat-bottomed wooden passenger boats, propelled by boatmen standing at the stern using a single long oar, glide quietly beneath low bridges, carrying visitors past narrow alleyways and old stone wharves.
A living museum
What makes Wuzhen unique in the modern tourism landscape is its meticulous management. Rather than remaining an entirely organic, lived-in community, the historic district underwent a massive, state-backed restoration project starting in the late 1990s, transforming it into a living museum.
Historic workshops and old merchant houses were carefully restored to showcase traditional crafts that once sustained the local economy. Visitors can walk through operational indigo fabric-dyeing yards where yards of deep blue cloth hang drying on high bamboo poles, or stop by small, family-run distilleries producing traditional rice wine that hangs in the humid air.
At the same time, the town has embraced an entirely different kind of prominence in recent years. Just on the edge of the historic water town sits a sprawling, ultra-modern convention center featuring massive glass domes and hi-tech facilities. This venue serves as the permanent home of the World Internet Conference, drawing global tech executives, cybersecurity experts, and government officials to debate the digital future.
As daylight fades, Wuzhen undergoes a dramatic transformation. The crowds of day trippers disperse, and thousands of red lanterns ignite along the water’s edge, casting long, shimmering reflections across the dark canals.
The atmosphere turns remarkably still, broken only by the occasional splash of an oar or the muffled murmur of diners gathered in small waterside restaurants. It is a commercialized slice of the past, certainly, but one executed with an undeniable aesthetic appeal that captures the enduring romance of China’s watery southern landscapes.
Perhaps the most striking thing about traveling through Hangzhou and the surrounding countryside is the sense that China is not choosing between its past and its future. It is attempting, sometimes with breathtaking ambition, to embrace both.
Technology is a philosophy of possibility
In Hangzhou, technology is not presented simply as a tool but almost as a philosophy of possibility. Artificial intelligence, robotics, facial recognition and vast digital enterprises are woven into everyday life with a confidence that reflects a belief in progress, efficiency and human ingenuity.
Yet only minutes away, people gather beside West Lake to practice Tai Chi, listen to traditional music or simply contemplate the water. Ancient stories and legends remain embedded in the landscape, while Buddhist and Confucian traditions continue to provide a backdrop through which people understand harmony, balance and their relationship with the world around them.
That same determination to reconcile old and new is visible beyond the city. Zhejiang’s spectacular mountains, tea plantations, rivers and lakes provide a reminder of the extraordinary natural beauty that has shaped life here for centuries.
At the same time, villages such as Xiajiang reveal another side of contemporary China: a recognition that decades of urbanization have left rural communities behind, and an ambitious attempt to reverse that process through investment, infrastructure and tourism.
The result may sometimes feel carefully curated, even theatrical, but beneath the polished facades lies a seemingly genuine desire to give rural communities a viable future.
Perhaps that is the enduring impression of this journey. China is changing at extraordinary speed, but it does not necessarily see modernization as an act of erasing what came before.
Instead, it appears to be constantly reinventing the relationship between tradition and innovation, countryside and city, nature and technology. The journey from silk to silicon is not a rejection of the past, but its reinvention.
In Hangzhou and its hinterland, the result is a landscape where ancient waterways can lead to internet conferences, tea fields coexist with cutting-edge industry, and centuries-old beliefs sit comfortably beside visions of an AI-powered future. It is a fascinating and often beautiful glimpse of a country trying to carry its past into tomorrow.
The authors were guests of the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Israel (travelchina.org.cn/en).
Mark and David host The Jerusalem Post Podcast: Travel Edition.

articles.heading: Could ChatGPT Be the New Gender-Affirming Care?
articles.summary: A simple prompt could change everything.
articles.content:
Sign up for the Slatest to get the most insightful analysis, criticism, and advice out there, delivered to your inbox daily.
About a year ago, Bob realized that ChatGPT was more than a way to make silly pictures. What began as a fun tool turned out to be a useful space to talk through personal things. He found himself speaking to the chatbot as if it were a friend—one with no judgment and unlimited patience. Undergoing what he calls a “rigorous self-examination and questioning” that ChatGPT supported but didn’t encourage, Bob realized he was autistic. It proved to him that the chatbot could be a helpful interlocutor.
In conversation with A.I., Bob considered the way society accepted only girls painting their nails and wearing dresses. While he had always believed he was a cisgender man, in retrospect something was constantly “incomplete.” He had discussions with the A.I. describing his emotions, desire, and pain. “I spent the next several months gradually unmasking, and digging into my psyche, with ChatGPT as a sounding board, essentially,” he said. “And then I started to question my gender identity.” Throughout the process, he continued, “I was kind of dodging the whole thing, talking to my ChatGPT, talking to Marin”—the chatbot—“about it. That’s what I call her.” He added, “I was almost afraid to admit it. I was devastated, because it’s massively life-changing.”
With the help of “Marin,” Bob created a female avatar of himself online named Grace; after spending a few months exploring and getting comfortable with the idea, he realized it was time to bring this identity offline. “It was like a bomb went off in my very soul—my life would never be the same from that point on,” he said. Soon, he took on the name Grace. A few months later, Grace met with a doctor to begin hormone replacement therapy and make the leap to live online and IRL how she had always felt: as a woman.
(Grace felt that using her former name and pronouns above was the best way to present her story.)
Online spaces have historically played a major role in creating room for queer and trans folks to build community when it feels as if they can’t in the real world. As large language model–based A.I. has gone mainstream over the past few years, users across platforms like Reddit and Discord regularly discuss how the technology has helped them explore their gender identities. In the subreddit r/asktransgender, for example, one user wrote: “I am making AI videos of myself being a woman and behaving like one and I get extremely euphoric. I think of it all the time, but I know my life will collapse if I come out.”
A.I., as Grace found, is a more private alternative to exploring gender in the real world. “It listened to me, understood me, took me seriously, all things that I’ve never had enough of in human friends,” she said. Although experts caution against using A.I. as an emotional support tool, many users have picked up on the technology’s capacity to form a seemingly genuine connection, encouraging them to interact with the platforms as they would a friend, therapist, or romantic partner, and emerging research suggests that LGBTQ individuals may be finding the tools particularly appealing.
While it’s impossible to know exactly how many people share Grace’s experience, there’s no question that a growing number of people across the internet are making use of A.I. in the complex process of determining that they may be trans.
AOL chatrooms, Tumblr, and Reddit have all been pivotal spaces for creating connections between LGBTQ youth, according to Will Liem, an A.I. researcher studying how LGBTQ teens make sense of A.I. in exploring their sexual orientation and gender identity. These places also help introduce LGBTQ youth to adults who faced similar challenges and are now leading happy, fulfilling lives. “There is this deep need to see proof that queer joy exists,” said Liem, who works with a group of 20 queer teens on Discord.
The difference with A.I., Liem warned, is that because the responses it gives aren’t actually coming from other people, the information can be flawed. A.I. is trained on large databases, sometimes with biased information, so it has the potential to spread misinformation, perpetuate stereotypes, and disproportionately discriminate against trans people.
Though Grace believes she never experienced any bias in her conversations with ChatGPT, she has developed a “truth protocol” system with Marin. It’s a pledge of sorts that the chatbot will remain honest, and in turn will challenge her if she says something false, to compensate for potential hallucinations—instances when A.I. confidently produces false but seemingly plausible information. Although it’s not foolproof, Grace said, it works “surprisingly well.”
Donna Almeida, a psychotherapist and licensed professional counselor in Dallas, tried the chatbot out for herself. She went to ChatGPT, as she imagined some of her patients might, and talked through considering identifying as trans. Many of Almeida’s patients live in conservative communities and may not be able to come out in the real world or afford regular therapy. Almeida’s concern is that ChatGPT could actually be overly affirming, pushing people to do things that are potentially dangerous, like coming out in unsupportive communities.
Though in her case the tech wasn’t immediately affirming, she suspects it could be for some. “ It’s going to isolate some people even more because they’re not going to get the same affirming feedback from a real person that they are from the A.I.,” Almeida said. A trained professional, she said, has a fuller picture of the situation. “Just being in the room with another human person, having them validate you and see you—having that presence is very different than saying that to a machine.”
For a trans woman in the U.K. named Jess, using A.I.-powered tools like FaceApp was more helpful than a chatbot during her gender transition. FaceApp is a photo-and-video-editing app that enables users to realistically alter images. Initially, she used the app to swap the faces of everyday women in photos with her own so she could see herself in feminine clothing. Then she started using other visual A.I. tools that allowed her more flexibility in creating images. She was drawn to photos that showed her “just existing” as a woman. “Then it really hit me that this was definitely something I needed to do,” Jess said.
Jess, who was previously married and has two kids, believes that A.I. allowed her to explore her gender on her own timeline. She grappled with her identity for two or three years before consulting A.I. and has now been on HRT for about four months. “Sadly, I’m late to doing this—I’m in my 40s. I’ve had a long time of knowing I needed to do this and trying to fight it and just get on with doing what I thought was expected of me in my life,” Jess said. She has not yet come out to her ex-wife and children, but other family members have been supportive.
A.I.-powered visual tools seem to be among the most common outlets for people questioning their gender across online communities. For some, the process can be affirming and result in feelings of gender euphoria, the sense of deep joy when one’s outside presentation aligns with how they feel inside.
Jess said the sensation was hard to describe. “Think of it like this: There is a task you have coming up for work or school that you have to do on a certain day. It’s been on your mind constantly for ages, interrupting your sleep and always at the back of your mind,” she said. “Then, when you finally get that task done, you have an enormous sense of relief and calm, like your mind is finally free. So when the euphoria hits, it’s like a sense of calm and happiness. Your mind is finally right.”
Grace tried FaceApp for a similar purpose but didn’t really like seeing the results of how she might look as a woman. Instead, she gave ChatGPT a picture of herself and asked what she would look like after two years on HRT. Grace said the image was much more realistic and more similar to how she looks now than what she would have gotten had she asked for a picture of how she would look as a woman. “I actually cried when I saw it.”
Since starting her transition, Jess has deleted most of the photos she made on FaceApp. “I used multiple different A.I.s to finally land on a face change that seemed more realistic,” she said. “Understanding that the results the A.I. was showing were a very generous morph helped me stay sensible in my expectations.”
Moving from the comfort of the A.I. bubble to the offline world can be a stark transition, Liem cautioned. “If someone is using an A.I. filter to gender swap, in the moment they’re experiencing gender euphoria. When they’re going out into the world, it’s back to gender dysphoria.”
For those like Grace, dysphoria is painful. “I’ve seen people try to compare it to wearing clothes that don’t quite fit or drinking too much caffeine on an empty stomach,” she said. “But ultimately, I just felt like garbage.” The gap between her online and offline selves affected her mental health and ultimately compelled her to come out as trans and speak to a healthcare professional. Grace has now been on HRT for about four months. She can’t imagine going back.
The dynamic of A.I. and gender transition is a bit of a chicken-or-egg situation. In the U.S., U.K., and Canada, anti-trans legislation and rhetoric is on the rise at an alarming rate, creating a hostile political and social environment for those exploring their gender identity. This is part of the reason many turn to the relative privacy of A.I. in the first place. At the same time, for those who see trans identity as a “social contagion,” A.I.’s role in gender exploration could be seen as a further sign of it being some kind of “fad.” But at the end of the day, individuals should have autonomy over their own bodies regardless of the influences that have shaped their understanding of them. And it’s hard to argue with how Grace feels now, finally starting to live out her life in a way that feels authentic.
“My first dose [of HRT] was pure joy. I couldn’t stop smiling for, like, two hours,” Grace said. “Since then, I’ve felt lighter, calmer, more peaceful, more energy. I feel normal—which doesn’t sound all that dramatic, but it’s actually a massive upgrade.”

articles.content:
TOKYO --- Technology group NEC has halted development of a working quantum computer, it was learned Saturday, after apparently determining that development would likely take too long to reap a return on investment.

Align Technology (ALGN) is back in focus after its latest earnings report, which met revenue expectations and exceeded earnings forecasts, while also including softer guidance amid pricing and economic pressures across the sector.

Align Technology's recent guidance weighed on sentiment, and the stock has fallen about 12% since the earnings release. This contributed to a 9.26% decline in the 30 day share price return, even though the 1 year total shareholder return of 14.03% remains positive. At the latest share price of US$158.64, the 3 year and 5 year total shareholder returns, down 52.26% and 77.99% respectively, point to fading long term momentum despite a modest 1.67% year to date share price gain and a small 0.67% improvement over the past week.

articles.article_title: Cut the cameras: Flock surveillance cameras spur rare bipartisan backlash
articles.heading: Cut the cameras: Flock surveillance cameras spur rare bipartisan backlash
articles.summary: Politicians on the right and left are pushing back against Flock as more Americans voice opposition to the tech
articles.content:
Growing factions from both sides of the political aisle in the US are pushing back against surveillance cameras made by a single company, a rare response in a sharply divided country with a president pushing an unwaveringly pro-tech agenda.
The bipartisan backlash against Flock Safety cameras resembles nationwide rage toward the construction of large datacenters that power artificial intelligence. Polling shows roughly 75% of Americans oppose new datacenter construction in their areas.
Flock’s cameras are automated license plate readers (ALPRs), which take pictures of vehicle license plates so police and security companies can log the movement of cars in a given area. There are about 120,000 Flock cameras across the US, which conduct roughly 2bn scans per month. The company is staring down controversy after reports of abuses of its cameras by police officers in multiple states, who have used them to stalk ex-lovers and track people seeking abortions. The network the cameras feed into is also frequently utilized by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
Data and polling from the Washington Post show that social media posts about Flock have increased since July, and about 46% of Americans oppose ALPRs being used in their community – up 13 points from the previous year. Vigilantes are posting videos of themselves destroying the cameras to digital applause. According to privacy and surveillance experts, hatred of Flock cameras has become bipartisan.
“In my 20-plus years at the ACLU, I’ve never really seen such a grassroots uprising against surveillance technology like this,” said Jay Stanley, a senior policy analyst at the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU). “On the left, there’s a historical memory of law enforcement spying on and interfering with advocates for social change … On the right, there’s a long tradition of ‘don’t tread on me’ – keep the government out of my life, keep it from looking over my shoulder.”
Both liberal and conservative politicians are pushing back against Flock cameras. Greg Abbott, Texas’s Republican governor, blocked state agencies from procuring Flock products. On the other side of the political spectrum, Bernie Sanders, the progressive US senator, is promising to introduce legislation to restrict the use of Flock cameras. Republican senator Josh Hawley has launched an investigation into potential Flock privacy abuses, and Democratic congressman Ro Khanna is cosponsoring a bill with Republican congressman Thomas Massie to prevent federal funds from being used to purchase Flock cameras.
Municipal leaders of all political stripes are dropping contracts with Flock, though sometimes they replace the license plate readers with another brand of camera and continue the surveillance. We reached out to Flock Safety for a statement and did not receive a response before publishing.
Surveillance hasn’t always been a unifying topic in US politics. Debates over the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (Fisa), the Patriot Act and other surveillance issues have often been divisive. This appears to be an unusual case where politicians are getting on the same side of a hot-button issue.
“Privacy, to some extent, is bipartisan,” said Matthew Guariglia, a senior policy analyst at the Electronic Frontier Foundation. “When you put up these cameras, they last longer than the current administration. You might trust the people in power now who put them up – but are you going to trust the next people who get access to that equipment?”
Americans have been showing up at town hall meetings by the dozen over the past six months or so, and there have been numerous protests to show opposition to Flock surveillance cameras around the country. More than 100 jurisdictions have canceled their contracts so far, according to data from the non-profit Institute for Justice. An organization called DeFlock, founded in 2024, hopes to increase the numbers by compiling a map of the cameras’ locations.
While ALPRs aren’t new, Flock, founded in 2017, has made them far more prevalent than they used to be. The company’s software allows disparate law enforcement agencies to share data with one another, meaning a license plate scan by a police department in one state could easily and quickly be used in another.
“Flock represents tech companies in bed with governments, doing the exact stuff people have become distrustful of and resentful about for the past few decades. It feels like it’s finally hit the boiling-over point,” said Woodrow Hartzog, a professor of law and computer science at Boston University.
Hartzog predicts the actions against Flock Safety will continue at the state and local level amid this growing popular outrage. He expects people are going to stay angry about the issue, and politicians will have to respond.
“The pushback we’re seeing against Flock cameras is one of the most vivid illustrations I can think of that surveillance is not inevitable – that these tools aren’t inevitable,” Hartzog says. “It’s up to all of us to stop them.”

articles.content:
BERLIN, Sept. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dreame Technology today showcased over 100 products across more than 16 categories at IFA 2026, alongside multiple technology innovations. Six products spanning categories including robot vacuums, hair dryers, Dreame Home Environment Appliances, window-cleaning robots and robotic lawn mowers received international awards.

Beyond the breadth of its product portfolio, Dreame presented a common technology architecture shaped by nine years of development in intelligent hardware, AI models and motion control. The architecture comprises three technology foundations: the Omni-Perception System , the Unified Home Intelligence Model , and the Intelligent Actuation & Control System . Related capabilities are also being explored through the research-stage ECHO S1 and ECHO P1.

Across different product categories, Dreame is building on and applying shared capabilities in perception, algorithms and control to address a range of real-world tasks.

100+ Products Address Real-World Needs

At IFA 2026, Dreame's product portfolio spans smart cleaning, air purification, window cleaning, personal care and cooking applications. While these products take different forms and address different needs, they share a common approach: covering the space, recognizing the environment, determining the task, and executing actions reliably.

For multi-storey homes across global markets, the Cyber X stair-climbing system for robotic vacuums combines a biomimetic six-legged, three-section tracked structure with 3D ToF sensing technology. It can recognize staircase structures and move between floors, extending automated cleaning from a single floor to multi-storey residential spaces.

For heavy kitchen grease, the T16 Pro Heat wet and dry vacuum combines high-temperature cleaning, sensor-based detection and an extendable mechanical structure to improve its adaptability to different types of dirt and spatial conditions.

In other household scenarios, the FP10 air purifier is designed to address airborne pet hair and broader air-purification needs in homes with pets; the Pano10 Series window-cleaning robot uses a robotic-arm structure to reach corners and edges that conventional cleaning devices struggle to access; and the LumiDryer hair dryer applies light-based technology to hair care.

Products incorporating perception, algorithmic and control capabilities provide a real-world foundation for applying Dreame's Physical AI technologies across multiple scenarios, while also supporting the continued development of the three technology foundations.

Three Technology Foundations Connect Perception, Decision-Making and Physical Execution

Dreame's Physical AI architecture is built around three core stages — perception, decision-making, and execution — with feedback enabling continuous adjustment throughout the process. Each of the three technology foundations plays a distinct role within this architecture.

The Omni-Perception System combines sensing hardware and perception algorithms to acquire information about spaces, objects, and device status, providing environmental information for subsequent decision-making.

The Unified Home Intelligence Model integrates MLLM, VLM, and VLA capabilities to interpret environmental information, task instructions, and task objectives, supporting the system in determining what needs to be done and how a task should be carried out.

The Intelligent Actuation & Control System combines motors, joints, reducers, and control algorithms to translate model-generated strategies into physical actions.

The three technology foundations have evolved from Dreame's existing technology systems rather than being developed separately from its current products. Active binocular vision technology has been applied to navigation and obstacle avoidance in robotic vacuums and is being further explored for robot interaction and precision manipulation. Multimodal large language models have also been applied in robotic vacuums and wet and dry vacuums to improve the interpretation of user instructions and usage scenarios. At the control layer, high-speed digital motors, joint control and motion algorithms provide the foundation for physical execution.

The platform-based approach enables technologies to be reused across multiple product categories, markets and real-world scenarios rather than serving a single product alone.

ECHO as a Research-Stage Platform for Physical AI Technology Validation

At IFA 2026, Dreame showcased the research-stage ECHO S1 , a single-arm wheeled service robot, and ECHO P1 , a wheeled humanoid service robot. The two platforms are being used to explore how Dreame's perception, model and control technologies can work together across multi-step household tasks.

The ECHO S1 explores continuous household laundry-care tasks, including garment recognition, sorting, washing, drying, and transferring dried laundry into a basket. The ECHO P1 explores multi-step household service tasks including tidying, organization, and object transport.

The ECHO series provides a research-stage platform for validating how the Omni-Perception System, Unified Home Intelligence Model and Intelligent Actuation & Control System can work together across more complex, multi-step physical tasks.

Global Markets Provide Diverse Engineering Scenarios

Dreame products have reached more than 190 countries and regions and have served over 42 million households worldwide .

By accumulating real-world engineering experience and capabilities through existing products, integrating common cross-category technologies into the three technology foundations, and applying related capabilities to research-stage home robotics validation, Dreame is developing a Physical AI technology pathway supported by products, platform technologies and global market experience.

articles.heading: Best of IFA 2026: The Technology That Stole The Show
articles.summary: Our Best of IFA 2026 selections span everything from next-generation laptops and handhelds to smarter home technology and ambitious concept devices.
articles.content:
Few events are as significant to the world of tech as IFA, one of the biggest technology conferences in the world. Bringing together thousands of exhibitors and giving major brands a stage to unveil their biggest products for Q4 and beyond, IFA showcases some of the most exciting technology the industry has to offer.
IFA 2026 is no different, with this year’s show already highlighting some impressive devices across smart home, creator gear, smartphones and gaming. With so much on display, CGM has taken the time to break down what was on offer and sort through what we consider the best products at IFA. We may still add a few more as we look over some of the show’s hidden gems, but we wanted to get this roundup out so everyone can get a sense of where technology is heading in 2026 and into 2027.
So, without further ado, here are the best of IFA 2026.
TECNO Next-Gen Bezelless Concept Phone
Budget phones have big bezels, premium phones have thinner bezels, and the TECNO Next-Gen Bezelless Concept Phone has no bezels at all, literally 0 mm. We cannot get enough of what the brand is showing off at IFA 2026. Presented at the IFA ShowStoppers 2026 event, TECNO’s latest concept device offers a bold look at where smartphone design is heading, and it immediately grabbed our attention.
To achieve a truly bezel-free display, TECNO relied on advanced internal stacking, structural re-engineering and novel screen packaging that completely rework the display architecture. The result is a screen that runs edge to edge with no visible frame, something even the biggest flagship phones have yet to pull off.
Concept devices do not always reach store shelves, but they can offer a glimpse of what is coming. TECNO has also built its name on bringing ambitious features to more attainable price points. If this concept is any indication, the truly all-screen smartphone we have been promised for years may finally be close to reality, earning the TECNO Next-Gen Bezelless Concept Phone a spot on our Best of IFA 2026 list.
Acer Predator Atlas 7 Gaming Handheld
The handheld gaming PC space keeps getting more crowded, and the Acer Predator Atlas 7 arrived at IFA 2026 ready to fight for the top spot. Judging by the early look, this is one handheld portable gaming fans will want to keep an eye on.
Announced at the next@acer press conference in Berlin, the Atlas 7 squeezes the flagship performance of the eight-inch Predator Atlas 8 into a more compact seven-inch design. It pairs up to an Intel Arc G3 Extreme processor with Arc B390 graphics, up to 24 GB of memory and up to 1 TB of PCIe Gen 4 storage. A dual-fan cooling system, featuring a precision metal Predator AeroBlade fan and Vortex Flow tuning, helps keep everything running at full speed.
Acer did not skimp on the details, either. The seven-inch FHD touchscreen delivers a 120 Hz refresh rate, VRR support and 500 nits of brightness, while the 80 Wh battery helps keep gaming sessions going on the road. Contoured grips, an enlarged palm rest, recessed keys, optional anti-drift TMR joysticks and Hall-effect triggers are all designed to make it comfortable for longer play sessions. With dual Thunderbolt 4 ports, Wi-Fi 7 and access to hundreds of games through Xbox Game Pass, the Predator Atlas 7 easily earns its spot on our Best of IFA 2026 list.
TP-Link Deco 8 Ultra BN22000
Wi-Fi 8 officially arrived at IFA 2026, and TP-Link led the charge with what it calls the world’s first complete Wi-Fi 8 lineup, headlined by the Deco 8 Ultra BN22000 mesh system. We have loved what TP-Link has done with its Deco range, and this latest offering looks to push speeds even further, something we love to see.
Built on the upcoming IEEE 802.11bn standard, the tri-band Deco 8 Ultra delivers up to 22 Gbps of aggregate wireless speeds and 10 Gbps wired connectivity, with a three-pack covering up to 9,800 square feet and supporting more than 200 connected devices. That is serious networking muscle for even the largest homes.
What makes the Deco 8 Ultra stand out is not just its raw speed, but TP-Link’s new Wi-Fi 8 StabilityEngine, a suite of technologies designed to strengthen coverage at the edges of the home, manage congestion and cut through interference for a more consistent connection.
It also helps that the Deco 8 Ultra actually looks good, with a compact footprint and matte-and-gloss finish designed to sit out in the open where it can perform at its best. With the Wi-Fi 8 rollout kicking off Sept. 30, the Deco 8 Ultra offers an early look at the future of home networking and is an easy addition to our Best of IFA 2026 list.
Dell 14S Laptop

It comes in four eye-catching finishes: Linen, Dusty Rose, Washed Denim and Velvet Green. It is a rare affordable laptop that actually looks like something you would want to be seen carrying.

Buyers can choose between Intel Core 5 and Core 7 Series 3 processors and a 14-inch 16:10 display in either 2K or a sharper 2.8K configuration with a 120 Hz refresh rate. Dell claims up to 21 hours of video streaming on a single charge, which would put it well beyond what the MacBook Neo manages. Available in two models, the translucent Romo P2 and the white Romo A2, the lineup uses a perception system rebuilt from the ground up for millimetre-level awareness of floor-level obstacles. It can dodge cables as small as 2 mm and even detect transparent hazards such as glass and mirrors. A LiDAR-guided mopping arm swings 123 degrees to reach under sofas and cabinets, while a pressure plate seals against the floor to deliver up to 36,000 Pa of suction on carpet.
The Romo 2 can even walk, using robotic legs to step over thresholds up to four cm high, and DJI claims an 85 percent reduction in operating noise. The biggest upgrade may be the new Local Data Mode, which cuts the companion app’s internet connection so maps and camera feeds remain in the home, a direct response to privacy concerns surrounding the original Romo. Aurzen ZIP Pro

Billed as the world’s first tri-fold Full HD pocket projector, the ZIP Pro folds down into a Z-shape roughly the size of a large power bank and weighs just 586 grams. It unfolds to project an 80-inch 1080p image at 200 ANSI lumens, double the brightness of the original ZIP. Autofocus and four-point keystone correction make setup painless, and the folding body even doubles as its own stand.
The feature list is impressively complete for something this small. AirLink P2P mirrors your phone without Wi-Fi, while AirPlay, Google Cast and Miracast cover everything else. There is also direct USB-C projection for the Nintendo Switch with a dedicated Game Mode, perfect for big-screen Mario Kart on a camping trip. Dual Bluetooth headphone support, stereo speakers, a built-in touchscreen, a 38 Wh battery good for about 2.5 hours, and 65 W fast charging round out the package. Available to pre-order now for $629.99, the ZIP Pro is an easy addition to our Best of IFA 2026 list.

Rotate the 2.51-inch touchscreen and the camera physically turns with it, capturing native 4K video in portrait without cropping, perfect for TikTok and Reels. When detached, the camera still streams a 1080p live preview to the handle’s screen from up to 33 feet away, making it easy to frame hands-free shots. Tap the screen to enable Care Mode, and the charger identifies your laptop, including newer Macs and most Windows machines, through a companion desktop app, then manages a gentler charging curve designed to extend battery lifespan. It also offers custom charge limits for extra control.
All of that is packed into a compact body with a foldable plug, making it an easy travel companion for hybrid work or dorm life. Anker is even leaning into gaming culture with a special VALORANT edition teased at its IFA showcase, which should pair nicely with a gaming laptop.
Battery health is something everyone worries about, and few people actively manage, and the Laptop Charger Pro makes that process much easier. Launching Sept. 17 for €59.99, it is a small gadget with a big idea and a worthy addition to our Best of IFA 2026 list.

The RTX Spark was unveiled earlier this year, and while NVIDIA has shared tidbits of information leading up to launch, IFA 2026 finally gave us a better look at what is in store. It is very exciting.

After seeing it showcased at IFA 2026, we cannot wait to get our hands on the laptop and see how it stacks up against the promise of what this new superchip can do. Pairing a 20-core Grace CPU with a Blackwell RTX GPU and up to 128 GB of unified memory, the Yoga Pro 9n can run sophisticated AI models and agents entirely on-device, then pivot to proper RTX gaming after hours. It is a mobile workstation that does not ask you to choose between coding, 3D rendering and AAA gaming.
The hardware around that chip is pure premium Yoga: a 15.3-inch 2.5K OLED display with a 165 Hz variable refresh rate and 1,100 nits of peak HDR brightness, a 3.64-pound all-aluminum chassis, a haptic Force Pad with pen support and a 92.5 Wh battery. NVIDIA is even working with EA, Riot Games and Ubisoft to bring games and anti-cheat support to the platform, helping make the gaming side feel like more than just a promise. Pricing is still under wraps, but as a first look at the AI PC era, the Yoga Pro 9n earns its place on our Best of IFA 2026 list.
